correctness.rationale: Hamming distance equals Lucas-cube distance by deletion-then-addition of independent sets. Every geodesic flips each coordinate at most once. Selected edges project onto distinct incident spokes 000-100, 000-010, 000-001; the projected geodesic is simple and cannot include all three. Counting edge families uses independent sets of paths of n-3 and n-4 vertices: F_{n-1}+2F_{n-2}=L_{n-1}. The embedded checker independently enumerated all shortest paths for n=5,...,9; no finite-to-infinite leap is used.

value.rationale: The 2023 motivating paper shows an isolated failure at n=5 of its union-of-two-theta-class lower bound, but no infinite stronger Lucas result. A transparent three-spoke structural obstruction gives a uniform all-dimension witness that exceeds 2F_{n-1} by the exponentially growing F_{n-4}; the limiting ratio is sqrt(5)/2. This is a motivated structural improvement, not a routine parameter substitution or finite table recalculation. It does not claim arbitrary-dimensional optimality.
